description: Creates a machine quote for a count: the records you would receive after removing ones already held and suppressed, the credits and GBP price, the licence, the warranty and any blockers. The quote_id lasts 24 hours and is bound to the dataset version; it is not a human sales quote, which is a 14 day PDF made in the app. Free and needs no account, and nothing is charged. Show the credits and price to the user, then call create_order with the quote_id. Lawful basis is UK GDPR Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interests; email audiences include corporate subscribers only by default (PECR), so sole traders and ordinary partnerships are left out unless the toggle is changed.

inputSchema.description: What to price: a count, a field set, how many records and the licence. Free, and needs no account.

connection_id.description: The CRM connection to check, only with dedupe_against crm or previous_orders_and_crm.

count_id.description: A count id from POST /v1/counts or count_audience. Either case is accepted; responses use upper case.

dedupe_against.description: Remove records you already hold: from earlier orders, from a connected CRM, or both. Default previous_orders when signed in. crm and previous_orders_and_crm need connection_id.

field_set.description: A field set id from GET /v1/field-sets, such as standard.

licence.description: multi_use_12m (12 month multi-use, every plan) or outright (1.8 credits a record, proposed).

limit.description: Records to buy; left out, the whole count.

name: quote_order

Licence.description: Licence terms as data, on every quote, order, records page and receipt. Records stay usable, pushable and re-downloadable free until reuse_until.

permitted_channels.description: email, telephone and post on standard terms.

reuse_until.description: Order date plus 12 months; null for outright.

terms_url.description: Where that version of the Data Licence and Sharing Agreement is published.

terms_version.description: The version of the Data Licence and Sharing Agreement the licence is under, such as 1.0.

type.description: multi_use_12m (12 month multi-use, every plan) or outright (1.8 credits a record, proposed).

Purchase.description: How to buy the credits the order needs, worked out by one function (cheapestPurchase) everywhere a price is shown. The caller's own, like the balance: read fresh on every read of the quote.

cheapest.description: The id of the cheapest option; null when nothing needs buying.

credits_to_buy.description: credits_required less the balance: all of it when signed out, 0 when the balance covers the order.

gbp_ex_vat.description: What the cheapest option costs, excluding VAT; 0 when nothing needs buying.

options.description: Cheapest first: the per-contact scale, and the credit pack (with any rest at the scale) when it is on sale. At the same price, the option that buys more credits comes first.

PurchaseLine.description: One thing bought: credit packs, or credits at the scale.

gbp_ex_vat.description: Pounds sterling excluding VAT, to two decimal places.

id.description: A credit pack id, or per_contact_scale.

quantity.description: Credit packs bought, or credits bought at the scale.

PurchaseOption.description: One way to buy the credits the order needs.

credits_left_over.description: Credits that stay in the balance after the order.

gbp_ex_vat.description: Pounds sterling excluding VAT, to two decimal places.

id.description: per_contact_scale, or the id of the credit pack the option is built on (with any rest at the scale). The same between quotes, so a choice survives a fresh quote.

QuoteBlocker.description: Something that stops create_order until it is fixed.

QuoteSignature.description: The signature over the machine quote's price, so an agent can hand the quote to another agent and both can check it. Verify it with the key at jwks_url.

jws.description: A compact JWS whose payload is the quote's id, organisation_id, count_id, dataset_version, records, credits_required, gbp_ex_vat, licence, expires_at.

kid.description: The signing key id in jwks_url.

Warranty.description: The bounce warranty that covers delivered records, with the threshold it was issued under.

policy.description: replace_over_threshold_hard_bounce is the current policy: records are replaced when hard bounces exceed threshold_percent of an order. replace_any_hard_bounce_30d is proposed and not yet in force. The current policy's id replaced one that named the threshold, a change to this public enum made before v2 went live.

threshold_percent.description: replace_over_threshold_hard_bounce only, and required there: the share of an order, in percent, that hard bounces must exceed before records are replaced. It is the threshold the document was issued under.

outputSchema.description: A machine quote: a signed price, valid 24 hours, bound to a dataset version and an organisation. create_order needs its id plus a human confirmation or a pre-authorised agent key; a confirmed flag set by a model is never consent.

balance_after.description: credits_available less credits_required; negative means a top-up is needed; null when signed out.

count_id.description: The count the quote was priced from.

anyOf.description: Credits, to one decimal place: whole at 1 credit a record, fractional only where a rule is (0.1 company-only, 1.8 outright, both proposed).

credits_available.description: Your balance; null when signed out.

credits_per_record.description: 1 for a complete UK record; 1.8 outright (proposed).

dataset.description: The dataset an audience draws from. uk_contacts is live; ie_contacts and global_contacts are listed but not yet served.

dataset_version.description: The immutable weekly build a count is bound to, such as 2026-W39. The last 52 stay queryable.

gbp_ex_vat.description: What credits_required cost bought the cheapest way, at the per-contact scale or with credit packs, excluding VAT. The same for every caller; purchase says what this caller needs to buy.

id.description: Format: a quote id: qte_ followed by a 26 character ULID in upper case Crockford base32, such as qte_01JB4M2R6T1Y5W8ZAK8Q2V7XN3.

anyOf.description: Format: an organisation id: org_ followed by a 26 character ULID in upper case Crockford base32, such as org_01JA0Q2V7XN3M9R6T1Y5W8ZAK8.

organisation_id.description: The organisation the quote belongs to; create_order settles it only there. null for a quote made without an account, which the first organisation to confirm it takes.

records.description: Records after overlap and suppression; what you would receive.

removed.description: Records left out and never charged.

title: Quote an order
